newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power firms on chilly weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power firms on chilly weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast firmed Monday on prospect of chilly weather staying in the region for the remainder of the week.

For Tuesday, the Southeast excluding Florida was predicted to experience temperatures in the 30s-50s Fahrenheit in the afternoon and teens to 30s at night. The Florida pennisula was forecast to enjoy day temperatures in the 60s-70s and night temperatures in the 30s-60s.
The latest outlook showed colder-than-normal weather would start to moderate toward the end of the week.

Peak, firm power for Tuesday delivery into northwestern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory were valued near $24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), with deals heard done as high as $27.00. Today's quote compared with Friday's $20.50 for Monday delivery.
Firm, next-day power for delivery into northwestern TVA during Tuesday's light load hours was notationally pegged near $18.00, up from Friday's $16.00.
Unconfirmed reports of outages at several coal-fired units in the Midwest bolstered daily prices at northwestern TVA, marketers said.
"A few coal units tripped off line over the weekend," said a Southeast trader.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices for Tuesday was mostly discussed near $25.00 range, compared with Friday's quote near $24.00. Offers was heard as high as $28.00-$29.00.
Firm, off-peak at the Ga./Fla. border for next-day delivery was held steady in the $16.00-$18.00 area.
Marketers expect prices in the Southeast to climb higher when level of trading returns to normal Tuesday.
"Tomorrow, we'll see a lot of the same," said a Houston marketer.
